info.title: QuBe Sync API
info.description: Integrate with QuickBooks Desktop or QuickBooks Enterprise in a few steps.

get.description: Returns a list of all connections for the authenticated application

post.description: Creates and returns a new connection for the authenticated application. Returns an onboarding URL for the user to complete the QuickBooks setup process. Only `name`, `redirect_url` and `type` can be set: sending `username`, `password`, `company_file`, `quickbooks_product_name` or `last_connected_at` is refused with `422` naming the field. Set a password with `POST /connections/{connection_id}/password`. A production app can have connections only once its organization has billing: until then every type is refused with `402 billing_required`.

name.description: Optional name for the connection - if you leave this blank, the company name returned by QuickBooks will be used once the first request is processed. A blank name (empty or only whitespace) is stored as null, and surrounding whitespace is trimmed. A simulated connection left blank takes its simulated company's name (Simulated Company) straight away.

type.description: How QuickBooks is reached. 'simulated' creates a fake QuickBooks answered by QuBe Sync: connected immediately, no Web Connector, meant for development and tests (see the Quickstart). Simulated connections are in beta: they don't match real QuickBooks in every case yet.

402.description: `billing_required`: this is a production app, and its organization has no active billing yet. A production app can't have connections of any type, `simulated` included, until an owner of the organization sets up billing in the dashboard. Use the sandbox app to test before then. Nothing was saved.

errors.detail: This is a production app, and its organization doesn't have billing set up yet, so it can't have connections. An owner of the organization can set up billing in the QuBe Sync dashboard. To test before then, use the organization's sandbox app.

422.description: Invalid fields, such as a `type` that isn't one of the listed values, or a field that can't be set here, such as `last_connected_at`. `errors` names each one. Nothing was saved.

get.description: Returns a single connection by ID

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: ID of the connection to return

delete.description: Deletes a connection by ID. This will also delete all associated queued requests. The Web Connector on the QuickBooks computer keeps the app until someone removes it there. QuBe Sync answers its check-ins as an invalid login and tells it to check in only once a day.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: ID of the connection to delete

204.description: Connection and all associated data deleted successfully

get.summary: List queued requests for a connection
get.description: Returns a paginated list of queued requests for a specific connection, ordered by most recent first. The response includes metadata about pagination.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: ID of the connection

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Number of items per page (max 100)

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort by

parameters.name: sort_direction
parameters.description: Sort direction (asc/desc)

parameters.name: search_phrase
parameters.description: Search phrase to filter queued requests

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Filter by request state

parameters.name: webhook_state
parameters.description: Filter by webhook delivery state

200.description: A paginated list of queued requests

data.response_xml: <QBXML><QBXMLMsgsRs statusCode='0' statusSeverity='Info' statusMessage='Status OK'><CustomerQueryRs requestID='1' statusCode='0' statusSeverity='Info' statusMessage='Status OK'><CustomerRet><ListID>80000001-1234567890</ListID><Name>Sample Customer</Name></CustomerRet></CustomerQueryRs></QBXMLMsgsRs></QBXML>

post.description: Creates a new queued request for processing by the QuickBooks integration. The QuickBooks request itself can be in either XML (`request_xml`) or JSON (`request_json`) format. If a webhook URL is provided, the system will send a POST request to that URL with the result when the request is completed. Only `request_xml`, `request_json` and `webhook_url` can be set: sending `state`, `webhook_state`, `iteration_state`, `api_version`, `response_json`, `response_xml`, `webhook_error`, `webhook_attempts`, `connection` or `error` is refused with `422` naming the field, and nothing is queued. QuBe Sync sets those as the Web Connector and QuickBooks handle the request.

parameters.name: connection_id
parameters.description: ID of the connection that will process this request

jsonRequest.summary: Specify a QuickBooks request with JSON

xmlRequest.summary: Specify a QuickBooks request with XML

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific queued request, including its current state, request/response data, and any associated errors. This endpoint can be used to poll for request completion or to check the status of a long-running operation.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the queued request

200.description: Queued request found and returned successfully

data.response_xml: <QBXML><QBXMLMsgsRs statusCode='0' statusSeverity='Info' statusMessage='Status OK'><CustomerQueryRs requestID='1' statusCode='0' statusSeverity='Info' statusMessage='Status OK'><CustomerRet><ListID>80000001-1234567890</ListID><Name>Sample Customer</Name></CustomerRet></CustomerQueryRs></QBXMLMsgsRs></QBXML>

webhook_attempts.error: Failed to deliver webhook: Connection timeout

data.webhook_error: Failed to deliver webhook after 3 attempts

error.message: QuickBooks found an error when parsing the provided XML text stream.
error.user_message: The request sent to QuickBooks was invalid. Please let us know what you were trying to do when this error occurred.

410.description: The requested queued request has been deleted

delete.description: Permanently deletes a queued request by ID. This operation is idempotent - deleting an already deleted request will return a successful response. Only requests that are in a terminal state (completed, error, or discarded) can be deleted. Active requests must be cancelled first.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the queued request to delete

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: If true, allows deletion of requests that are not in a terminal state. Use with caution as this may leave the connection in an inconsistent state.

204.description: Queued request was successfully deleted or did not exist

400.description: Bad request - cannot delete request in current state

error.message: Cannot delete request in state 'waiting'. Only completed, failed, or discarded requests can be deleted.

404.description: Queued request not found or already deleted

409.description: Conflict - cannot delete request due to business rules

connectionActive.summary: Cannot delete request with active connection

error.message: Cannot delete request: Connection is currently active. Please disconnect first.

200.description: Onboarding URL regenerated successfully. The full connection object is returned, with updated `links.onboarding` URL.

apiKey.description: Use your app's API_KEY as the username, and leave the password blank

connection_redirect_url.description:
The URL to redirect the user to after they complete (or cancel) the QuickBooks setup process. This URL should be able to handle the query parameters:
 * `?state=connected` if they completed the process,
 * `?state=cancelled` if they cancelled it or
 * `?state=expired` if they visit the onboarding link after it has expired

last_connected_at.description: Timestamp of when the connection was last used

app_id.description: ID of the app this connection belongs to

company_file.description: Name of the QuickBooks company file

username.description: Automatically generated username for the connection

qbxml_version.description: The latest QBXML version supported by the connected QuickBooks instance

quickbooks_product_name.description: The product name of the connected QuickBooks instance

type.description: How QuickBooks is reached: 'standard' (Web Connector every 5 minutes), 'realtime' (every 10 seconds) or 'simulated' (a fake QuickBooks answered by QuBe Sync itself, for development and tests; in beta: it doesn't match real QuickBooks in every case yet).

company_file.description: Name of the QuickBooks company file

id.description: Unique identifier for the queued request

state.description: Current state of the queued request. `timed_out`: no answer came back (the customer's computer lost its connection, or QuickBooks or the Web Connector was closed, mid-request), so QuickBooks may still have applied it. `discarded`: it was discarded before the Web Connector picked it up, so QuickBooks never got it.

webhook_state.description: State of the webhook delivery. Not applicable if webhook_url was not provided.

request_xml.description: The QBXML request to be processed

request_json.description: The request payload in JSON format (alternative to request_xml)

response_xml.example: <QBXML><QBXMLMsgsRs statusCode='0' statusSeverity='Info' statusMessage='Status OK'><CustomerQueryRs requestID='1' statusCode='0' statusSeverity='Info' statusMessage='Status OK'><CustomerRet><ListID>80000001-1234567890</ListID><Name>Sample Customer</Name></CustomerRet></CustomerQueryRs></QBXMLMsgsRs></QBXML>
response_xml.description: The QBXML response from QuickBooks. One answer can be at most 4 MB as the Web Connector sends it, about 3 MB of qbXML; QuickBooks' answer over that isn't kept: this is null and `error.error_type` is `response_too_large`.

response_json.description: The response payload in JSON format, if request is completed: QuickBooks' qbXML answer as JSON, element for element. Each `*Rs` element carries QuickBooks' `@statusCode`, `@statusSeverity` and `@statusMessage`. `Info` is a success. `Warn` means QuickBooks carried the request out but warned about something, and the `*Ret` it answered with is still there: for example `@statusCode` 530, `The field "Memo" is not supported by this implementation.`, means the record was saved without that field. `Error` means QuickBooks refused it.

webhook_url.description: URL to receive a webhook when the request is completed. The webhook carries the request as it then is, `response_xml` and `response_json` included, so it is at most about twice the size limit on one answer (see `response_xml`).

status.description: Whether the webhook endpoint accepted this delivery (a 2xx answer)

error.description: Why the delivery failed (`null` when it succeeded)

attempted_at.description: Not sent: the time of an attempt is `sent_at`

response.description: Not sent: the outcome of an attempt is `status`, and a failure's reason is `error`

webhook_attempts.description: Every webhook delivery attempt for this request, newest first

webhook_error.description: Error message if webhook delivery failed

error_type.description: Where it failed. `timed_out`: no answer came back, and QuickBooks may still have applied the request, so look before sending it again. `discarded`: QuickBooks never got it. `response_too_large`: QuickBooks answered, but with more than QuBe Sync accepts for one answer (4 MB as the Web Connector sends it, about 3 MB of qbXML), so `response_xml` and `response_json` are null. QuickBooks ran the request: page the query (`iterate`, or `iterator="Start"` with `<MaxReturned>` in `request_xml`) or narrow it, and for a write, look before sending it again.

message.description: The raw message from QuickBooks or the Web Connector; for `timed_out` and `discarded`, which neither sent, QuBe Sync's own

user_message.description: A friendly message for the end user

error_code.description: QuickBooks' statusCode, for a business error

hresult.description: The Web Connector's HRESULT, for a connection or XML error

debug_message.description: Which element of the request the value came from, when known

code.description: Not sent: QuickBooks' status code is `error_code`

error.description: Set when `state` is `error`, `retryable`, `timed_out` or `discarded`. A `timed_out` request's `error_type` is `timed_out`, and a `discarded` one's `discarded`, unless the request was `retryable` when it was discarded: then it keeps the connection error that held it up.

inserted_at.description: When the request was queued, UTC ISO 8601

updated_at.description: When the request was last updated

connection_id.description: ID of the connection this request belongs to

request_json.description: The request payload in JSON format (alternative to request_xml)

request_xml.description: The request payload in QBXML format (alternative to request_json)

webhook_url.description: Optional absolute http or https URL to receive a webhook when the request is completed. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address. A `qube listen` URL must be one of this app's.

max_returned.description: Maximum number of records to return

request_id.description: A custom ID that can be used to identify the request and response. This could be your local ID for the request.

iterate.description: If true, QuBe Sync will automatically handle the QBXML iteration until all records are returned. Each page of results will have its own request record and webhook. The id and webhook_url will be the same across each page request, and there will also be `page_request_id`, `page` values to distinguish pages from each other.

webhook_url.description: Optional absolute http or https URL to receive a webhook when the request is completed. It may not contain a username or password, and in production it may not point at localhost or a private, loopback or link-local address. A `qube listen` URL must be one of this app's.

Error.description: What a refused request answers with. The one key is errors, and its shape says what went wrong: a sentence when the endpoint explains the refusal in words (a parameter the operation does not take, a key already taken, a run that has already ended); an object with detail, and a code when there is one, when the request named nothing that exists or may not do what it asked (402, 403, 404, and a CLI session's 401), or an answer to a run's question was refused (the decisions endpoint's 400, 409 and 422, which always carry a code to branch on); an object of fields, each a list of messages, when a record failed validation and nothing was saved; a list of {path, message} problems when a submitted document or input fails validation. A request without a usable API key gets a 401 Basic challenge with the plain-text body Unauthorized, not JSON.

redirect_url: must not have a query string

ValidationErrors.description: A field-by-field list of what was wrong. Nothing was saved.

last_connected_at: is read-only: QuBe Sync sets it from the Web Connector and QuickBooks

Unauthorized.description: No usable API key. The key is Basic auth, so the answer is the challenge, with the plain-text body Unauthorized rather than JSON.

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found

UnprocessableEntity.description: A field failed validation, field by field, and nothing was queued: such as a `webhook_url` that is not an absolute http or https URL, carries a username or password, or (in production) points at localhost or a private address.

webhook_url: must be an http or https URL

tags.name: Pre-built Queries
tags.description: Endpoints for executing pre-built queries against QuickBooks data. These endpoints simplify common data retrieval operations by providing a higher-level interface than the raw queued requests API. Each query is executed asynchronously and returns a queued request ID that can be used to check the status and retrieve results.
